To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ATP-induced internalization of large macronolecules in living cells occurs in two stages: (a) ATP induces poration of the cell membrane, (b) ATP-induced poration of the plasma membrane is followed by a sorting process which sorts out the membrane from the internalized macromolecules.

ATP-induced internalization of large macronolecules occurs in human Chang liver cell line, and the internalized macromolecules are seen in two different sites, viz. (1) inside vacuole and (2) outside vacuole, in the cytoplasm.

(i) ATP-induced internalization of large macronolecules (2,000,00 mol. wt. dextrans, 0.92 and 2.1 microns latex beads) occurs in human Chang liver (HCL) cells; and (ii) ATP-induced internalized beads are distributed in two distinct sites, viz. inside vacuoles (endocytotic entry) and outside vacuoles (cytosol) in the cytosolic region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the demonstration of the ability of ATP to induce internalization of macromolecules and particles in the living state.
the demonstration of ATP induced cytosolic penetration of large macromolecular particles, and the sorting out of these particles in the cell.
the mechanism of internalization of extracellular particles in human Chang liver hepatocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ATP induces internalization of large macronuclei in the living state, which is a novel and significant discovery in cell physiology.
ATP is capable of inducing the internalization of macromolecules of 0.9-2.2 micron diameter in the living state.
ATP is a potent inducer of cellular uptake of large macromolecular particles, and the process of internalization is a complex phenomenon involving endocytic and non-endocytic pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytosol can be accessed by extracellular macromolecules in a living state without perturbations.
the ATP-induced poration of the cell membrane is a two-stage process, viz. (1) the initial ATP-activated poration of membrane and (2) the sorting out of the membrane fragments.
extracellular ATP induces a transient poration in human Chang liver cell membrane, and that the pores are of the size that allows entry of 2, 000,000 mol wt dextran molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ATP can act as an extracellular signal molecule to trigger cellular events, such as internalization of macromolecules, in the living state.
the living cell is capable of internalizing large macromolecules, which is a hitherto unknown phenomenon in cell biology.
the ATP-induced internalization of the large macromolecules is a non-endocytic process, and the mechanism is still unclear.
